document_title: RBI Initiative: UPI for Feature Phones (UPI123Pay) and DigiSaathi Helpline
source_org: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
text: The Reserve Bank has launched two key initiatives today – (1) UPI123Pay – Option to make Unified Payments Interface (UPI) payments for feature phone users, and (2) DigiSaathi - a 24x7 Helpline to address the queries of digital payment users across products. While launching the two initiatives, RBI Governor Shri Shaktikanta Das highlighted the importance of these initiatives in enhancing the diversity, utility and transformational power of digital innovations in the country. These initiatives will further deepen the digital ecosystem and financial inclusion. The Governor also stated that the RBI stands committed to providing an enabling environment for this.

document_title: RBI Initiative: UPI for Feature Phones (UPI123Pay) and DigiSaathi Helpline
source_org: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
text:
At present, efficient access to UPI is available on smart phones. UPI can be accessed through NUUP (National Unified USSD Platform) using the short code of *99#. But this option is cumbersome and not popular. Considering that there are more than 40 crore feature phone mobile subscribers in the country, UPI123pay will materially improve the options for such users to access UPI. UPI123Pay includes four distinct options as below:

App-based Functionality : An app would be installed on the feature phone through which several UPI functions, available on smartphones, will also be available on feature phones.

document_title: RBI Initiative: UPI for Feature Phones (UPI123Pay) and DigiSaathi Helpline
source_org: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
text:
Missed Call : This will allow feature phone users to access their bank account and perform routine transactions such as receiving, transferring funds, regular purchases, bill payments, etc., by giving a missed call on the number displayed at the merchant outlet. The customer will receive an incoming call to authenticate the transaction by entering UPI PIN.

Interactive Voice Response (IVR) : UPI payment through pre-defined IVR numbers would require users to initiate a secured call from their feature phones to a predetermined number and complete UPI on-boarding formalities to be able to start making financial transactions without internet connection.

text: The 24x7 Helpline – ‘DigiSaathi’ – provides a channel to obtain help on the entire gamut of digital payments. Automated responses on information related to digital payment products and services are available in Hindi and English through multiple options like – (a) toll-free number (1800-891-3333), (b) a short code (14431), (c) website – www.digisaathi.info , and chatbots. DigiSaathi will assist users with their queries on digital payments via website & chatbot facility and through toll-free calls where user can dial or call out the options / products for which the information is required. More interactive options and language choices shall be enabled going forward.

document_title: RBI BE(A)WARE: Modus Operandi of Financial Frauds and Safe Digital Practices
source_org: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
text:
1. CORE GOLDEN RULES FOR FINANCIAL SAFETY:
- NEVER SHARE YOUR CONFIDENTIAL CREDENTIALS: Never share your OTP, UPI PIN, ATM PIN, Password, CVV, or Card Expiry Date with ANYONE.
- RBI OR BANK OFFICIALS NEVER ASK FOR PASSWORDS OR OTPS: Neither the RBI, banks, nor police officials ever call customers requesting OTPs or asking them to transfer money to "safe accounts".
- UPI PIN IS ONLY REQUIRED TO SEND MONEY: You DO NOT need to enter your UPI PIN to receive money. If someone asks you to enter your PIN or scan a QR code to receive a payment or refund, IT IS A SCAM.

2. COMMON FRAUD MODUS OPERANDI AND PREVENTIONS:

document_title: RBI BE(A)WARE: Modus Operandi of Financial Frauds and Safe Digital Practices
source_org: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
text:
A. PHISHING & VISHING (Voice Phishing):
- Modus Operandi: Fraudsters pose as bank managers, telecom operators, or electricity board agents claiming your account, SIM, or electricity will be disconnected unless you update KYC immediately via a link or app.
- Safeguard: Never click on unverified links sent via SMS, WhatsApp, or Telegram. Contact your local branch directly using official numbers printed on the back of your debit card.

document_title: RBI BE(A)WARE: Modus Operandi of Financial Frauds and Safe Digital Practices
source_org: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
text:
B. FAKE LOAN APPS:
- Modus Operandi: Unregulated mobile applications offer instant, collateral-free loans, obtain full access to phone contacts and photo galleries, charge extortionate interest rates, and resort to blackmail.
- Safeguard: Check the list of RBI-registered NBFCs and banks before downloading loan apps. Never grant contacts or media permissions to unverified loan apps.

document_title: RBI BE(A)WARE: Modus Operandi of Financial Frauds and Safe Digital Practices
source_org: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
text:
C. SIM SWAP FRAUD:
- Modus Operandi: Fraudsters acquire a duplicate SIM card in your name using fake KYC documents, intercepting your 2FA OTPs while your original SIM loses signal.
- Safeguard: If your mobile phone abruptly loses cellular network signal for an extended period, immediately contact your mobile network operator.

document_title: RBI BE(A)WARE: Modus Operandi of Financial Frauds and Safe Digital Practices
source_org: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
text:
D. WORK-FROM-HOME / SOCIAL MEDIA INVESTMENT SCHEMES:
- Modus Operandi: Scammers recruit victims via Telegram or WhatsApp offering high part-time pay for rating movies, liking YouTube videos, or trading crypto. Initial small returns are paid to build trust, followed by demands for lakhs of rupees which are then frozen.
- Safeguard: Guaranteed high returns with zero risk do not exist in legitimate markets. Avoid unverified Telegram trading groups.

document_title: RBI BE(A)WARE: Modus Operandi of Financial Frauds and Safe Digital Practices
source_org: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
text:
3. IMMEDIATE ACTION UPON FACING FRAUD:
- Report within the Golden Hour: Immediately call the National Cyber Crime Helpline at 1930 or file a complaint at https://cybercrime.gov.in.
- Block Cards & Net Banking: Call your bank's toll-free number immediately to hotlist your card and freeze compromised bank accounts.

source_org: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
text:
RESERVE BANK OF INDIA — INTEGRATED OMBUDSMAN SCHEME (RB-IOS)
Official Source: Reserve Bank of India (Consumer Education and Protection Department)
Website: https://cms.rbi.org.in | Contact Center: 14448 (Toll-Free, 10+ Indian Languages)

1. WHAT IS THE INTEGRATED OMBUDSMAN SCHEME?
The Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme integrates erstwhile separate ombudsman schemes for Banks, NBFCs, and Non-Bank Prepaid Payment Instruments (PPIs) into 'One Nation One Ombudsman'. It provides a cost-free, expeditious resolution mechanism for customer grievances against RBI-regulated entities.

document_title: RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme: Grievance Redressal Mechanism & Customer Rights
source_org: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
text:
2. WHEN CAN A CUSTOMER FILE A COMPLAINT?
A customer can approach the RBI Ombudsman if:
(a) The regulated entity has rejected the complaint wholly or partly.
(b) The customer has not received any reply from the bank/NBFC within 30 days of filing the representation.
(c) The customer is dissatisfied with the reply given by the regulated entity.
Time Limit: The complaint must be lodged within 1 year from the date of receipt of the bank's rejection or expiry of the 30-day period.

document_title: RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme: Grievance Redressal Mechanism & Customer Rights
source_org: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
text:
3. VALID GROUNDS FOR COMPLAINTS:
- Delay or failure in processing inward/outward remittances (NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, UPI).
- ATM/Debit card/Credit card debit without cash dispense or unauthorized debit.
- Refusal to open deposit accounts without valid reason or non-adherence to KYC guidelines.
- Levying service charges without prior notice.
- Non-observance of RBI Fair Practices Code by lenders (harassment by recovery agents, lack of transparency in loan terms).
- Inordinate delays in loan sanctioning, disbursement, or return of property title deeds after loan repayment.
- Mobile/Internet banking transaction failures.

document_title: RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme: Grievance Redressal Mechanism & Customer Rights
source_org: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
text:
4. HOW TO LODGE A COMPLAINT:
- Online Portal: https://cms.rbi.org.in (24x7 web portal with tracking facility).
- Email: crpc@rbi.org.in
- Physical Post: Centralised Receipt and Processing Centre (CRPC), Reserve Bank of India, 4th Floor, Sector 17, Chandigarh - 160017.
- Contact Center: Dial 14448 (toll-free) for guidance and tracking.

5. COMPENSATION POWERS:
The Ombudsman can award compensation up to Rs. 20 lakh for actual consequential loss suffered, and up to Rs. 1 lakh for mental anguish, harassment, and loss of time.

Source: Reserve Bank of India Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) & Database on Indian Economy (DBIE)
Website: https://www.rbi.org.in | Frequency: Bi-monthly Monetary Policy Review

1. KEY POLICY BENCHMARK RATES (Current Observation):
- Policy Repo Rate: 5.50% (The rate at which RBI lends money to commercial banks against government securities).
- Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) Rate: 5.25% (Uncollateralized absorption of liquidity by RBI).
- Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) Rate: 5.75% (Penal borrowing rate for banks).
- Bank Rate: 5.75%.

document_title: RBI Macroeconomic Benchmarks: CPI Inflation Target and Policy Repo Rate
source_org: Reserve Bank of India (RBI Database / Monetary Policy)
text:
2. INFLATION TARGETING FRAMEWORK:
- Statutory Target: Under Section 45ZA of the RBI Act, the Central Government in consultation with the RBI set the Consumer Price Index (CPI) Combined inflation target at 4.0% with an upper tolerance band of 6.0% and a lower tolerance band of 2.0% (4% +/- 2%).
- Target Benchmark: CPI (Combined) Base Year 2012 = 100.
- Measurement Frequency: Published monthly by the National Statistical Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

document_title: RBI Macroeconomic Benchmarks: CPI Inflation Target and Policy Repo Rate
source_org: Reserve Bank of India (RBI Database / Monetary Policy)
text:
3. HOW INFLATION IMPACTS PERSONAL PURCHASING POWER:
- Purchasing power measures the quantity of goods or services that one unit of currency can buy.
- Positive inflation erodes purchasing power over time. If inflation averages 6.0% annually, a basket of goods costing Rs. 1,00,000 today will cost approximately Rs. 1,79,084 in 10 years.
- To protect wealth, financial planners recommend investing in asset classes (such as equity mutual funds or diversified portfolios) whose post-tax expected returns outpace the prevailing CPI inflation rate over long horizons.

Inflation effects on Investments 
While planning your invest ment, it is important to take into account the 
effects of inflation on your investments. Inflation is the rise in prices of 
goods and services. As the prices of goods and services increase, the 
value of rupee goes down and you will no t be able to purchase as much 
with those rupees as you could have in the last month or last year.

Say that your monthly consumption of petrol is 10 litres, costing you ` 500

the year is 10%, then price of petrol per litre would increase from ` 50 to ` 
55 / litre. Accordingly, the next year you will not be able to purchase 10 
litres of petrol, now costing ` 55 / litre, out your interest income of ` 500 
from your fixed deposit. Hence y our financial plan should aim to earn 
returns above the rate of inflation. e.

d. Pricing of (public) issues 
On the basis of pricing, issues can be classified into Book Built issues and Fixed Price 
issues. We shall focus on the book built issues as most of the issues nowadays are 
through this method. i. In a Book Building issue the issuer company mentions the minimum and 
maximum price (price band) at which it will sell (issue) its shares. Thus the offer 
document (in this case, called the Red Herring Prospectus ) contains only the 
price band instead of the price at which its shares are offered to the public. Within this price band the investor can choose the price at which the investor are 
willing to buy the shares and also the quantity.

broker’s (also called syndicate member ) terminal. The list of the bid received 
from investors at various price bands is known as the ‘ book’ and can be seen in

issuer and merchant banker.

IPO Grading 
 
1. What is IPO grading 
IPO grading is the professional assessment of a Credit Rating Agency 
(CRAs) on the fundamentals of a company in relation to the other listed equity 
shares in India. It is mandatory for the issuer company coming with initial 
public offer (IPO) to obtain IPO grading from a Credit Rating Agency and 
disclose the same on the cover page of offer document and Application 
form. IPO grading endeavors to provide the in vestor with an informed, objective 
independent and unbias ed opinion of a CRA after an alyzing various relevant 
factors. It is an additional input available for your investment decision.

document_title: SEBI Investor Guide: Primary Markets and Initial Public Offerings (IPO)

text:
An IPO grade is NOT a suggestion or recommendation as to whether an 
investor should subscrib e to the IPO or not. IPO grade needs to be read 
together with the disclosures made in the offer document including the risk 
factors as well as the price at which the shares are being offered. IPO grade does not take in to account the price of the shares being offered. Therefore, the investors need to make an ind ependent judgment regarding 
the price of the investment. 2.

Credit Rating 
1. What is credit rating 
Credit rating is an opinion of a Cr edit Rating Agency ( CRA) on the likelihood of 
timely payment of interest and principal (credit risk) on the rated debt instrument. It is an unbiased, objective, and independent assessment of the issuer's capacity 
to meet its financial obligations and is conveyed with alphanumeric symbols. Credit rating is not a recommendation to buy, sell or hold a debt instrument. It is a 
comment on the probability of the intere st and principal of a debt instrument 
being paid or not paid on time (credit risk).

investors are required to make your their independent and objective analysis 
before arriving at an investment decision. 2. How is it done? Each credit rating agency has its own set of criteria and di fferent weight age for 
each component for a ssigning the ratings. The indicative list of factors that are 
taken into consideration for credit ra ting are issuer com pany’s opera tional 
efficiency, its str engths and weakness, level of technological development, 
financials, competence an d effectiveness of management, past record of debt 
servicing, etc. The issuer pays for the credit rating. 3.
